findings.message: Citation support: topic-04.mdx (### Impact of computers and the internet on society) attributes to Bourgeois and colleagues (2019) that the digital divide "runs along income, geography, education, age and gender lines". The bound excerpt (specs/content/gict-300/sources/texts/bourgeois2019.md, chapter 11) supports income, geography, education and age (economic and usability dimensions; ACM list: low-income households, senior citizens, single-parent children, the undereducated, minorities, rural residents) but contains no gender dimension, so "gender" attributes to the source more than the bound text supports. Repair: delete "and gender" from the Bourgeois-attributed list, or move the gender observation out of the attribution (it is independently true and relevant in Pakistan and may stand as an unattributed contextual observation).

Figure defect: static/img/figures/gict-300/unit-01/fig-U1-6.svg and fig-U1-6.dark.svg (size-and-power ladder, topic 1.3) clip the bottom-right axis label: <text class="small" x="686" y="425">more specialised</text> extends to x=795.8, past the 780-unit viewBox right edge, so the rendered figure cuts the label mid-word ("more specialis"). Confirmed by scripts/measure-figure-text.mjs (15.7px overflow, both variants), render-inspect section D (both variants flagged) and the element screenshot render-inspect/fig-U1-6-label-corner.png. check:figures passes this silently because it measures no glyph geometry. The .ur.svg variants are clean. Repair: move the label left (e.g. text-anchor="end" anchored near the axis end at x=679) or shorten it, in BOTH light and dark variants, keeping the mirrored .ur.svg geometry consistent.

Sources-file accuracy: specs/content/gict-300/sources/unit-01.md preamble states every key is cited "both in prose and in a per-topic ## Further reading section", but hecICT (cited in topic-01 prose as "(HEC, n.d.)") appears in no Further reading list. The sources-consulted contract requires coverage-matrix consistency only, so no gate fails. Repair: add the HEC guidelines line to topic-01's Further reading or correct the preamble.

Declaration precision for the history sub-topics: the sources file's bourgeois2019 row claims "computing history context (U1-03)" and the khanacademyCIT declaration says the bound bourgeois2019 excerpt "independently supports" the standard history and hardware story, but the bound excerpt (chapters 1 and 11) contains no computing-history content; topic-02/03 Further reading cites bourgeois2019 chapter 2, which is not bound. The evolution/generations account itself is the standard one and was checked accurate (Pascal/Leibniz/Jacquard/Babbage/Hollerith/ENIAC 1946 ~27 tonnes/von Neumann 1945 stored-program/IBM PC and Apple II/iPhone 2007), and the prose discloses the bibliographic level of the guide-required citations, so this is a governance-wording blemish rather than learner-facing misattribution. Repair: reword the sources file to state that the history account rests on khanacademyCIT (catalogue-corroborated) and shellyVermaat at bibliographic level, or bind a chapter-2 excerpt.

Link text: Further reading citation links render as bare URLs as the link text on all four topic pages (render-inspect advisory observation; e.g. https://doi.org/10.2760/115376). Descriptive link text would serve screen-reader users better; the current repo convention for citation lists accepts bare URLs, so this is advisory.
